title: Coinbase–CFM–CBBM–Deribit XRP collateral pathway: legal and operational conditions
executive_conclusion: A concrete conditional route exists for customer-owned XRP to be accepted as 30.7 margin collateral by Coinbase Financial Markets and re-used through Coinbase Bermuda to Deribit. XRP qualifies as a digital commodity under the referenced March 2026 SEC/CFTC interpretation and is the underlying of a Coinbase Derivatives CFTC-registered DCM futures contract. Deribit lists XRP linear USDC options/perpetuals and lists XRP as cross-collateral in X:SM. This is not proof that CFM has enabled XRP collateral, that the initial three-month restriction has expired, or that any customer has posted XRP.

sequence.role: U.S. CFTC-registered FCM; holds customer positions and margin collateral on its books.
Foreign broker affiliate; receives 30.7 customer funds in an omnibus account and routes orders to Deribit; customer-level subaccounts are pseudonymized.
Foreign board of trade/foreign clearing organization; executes derivatives and receives margin under a right of re-use authorized by applicable local law/rules.

CFM represented that Deribit would maintain assets equal to 100% of net liquidating equity for the relevant CFM 30.7 customers in one or more accounts at this Coinbase-owned New York limited-purpose trust company.

facts: Coinbase said institutional clients could begin onboarding to global crypto derivatives through CFM.
Coinbase said options on Deribit were live through CFM.
Coinbase said contracts and collateral types would expand, with perpetual futures to follow.
product_status.limitation: This announcement does not name XRP as a collateral type enabled through CFM and does not disclose XRP balances or customer use.

digital_commodity_classification.evidence: CFTC Letter 26-17 footnote 5 identifies XRP among the examples of digital commodities in the March 2026 SEC/CFTC Digital Commodity Interpretation.

cftc_registered_dcm_futures_criterion.evidence: Coinbase Derivatives, LLC self-certified an XRP Futures contract on April 3, 2025 for listing on or after April 21, 2025. The contract is a monthly, USD-settled and margined futures contract, 10,000 XRP per contract, code XRL.
cftc_registered_dcm_futures_criterion.significance: CFTC Letter 26-05 condition 1.2 permits a non-stablecoin digital asset in a 30.7 customer account if it is the underlying commodity of a futures contract listed on a CFTC-registered DCM, subject to the remaining conditions.

conditions: The FCM must file a notice of intent with the Market Participants Division before relying on the no-action position and state the date it will begin accepting digital-asset collateral.
For the first three months from the FCM's stated commencement date, customer collateral is restricted to payment stablecoins, Bitcoin and Ether.
Before accepting a non-security digital asset other than Bitcoin, Ether or a payment stablecoin, the FCM must submit revised risk-management policies and procedures to MPD via WinJammer.

For a 30.7 customer account, if the asset is not accepted by a registered DCO or a qualifying foreign clearing organization, the FCM applies fair market value after a haircut of at least 20% for non-stablecoin digital assets.

If the asset is accepted by a qualifying registered DCO or foreign clearing organization, the applicable clearing organization's valuation and haircut rules apply; where multiple organizations accept it, the highest applicable haircut is used.

For a digital asset that is not a payment stablecoin, the special matched-currency haircut treatment only applies when the contract is both based on and denominated in that same digital asset and the collateral offsets a deficit in that contract.

The September 24, 2026 CFTC staff FAQ Q10 clarifies that the initial three-month restriction runs from the date the FCM first accepts crypto assets from customers; the notice must state the intended commencement date. Weekly reporting is a separate three-month period beginning with the calendar month after the notice month.

For non-security digital assets other than Bitcoin, Ether and payment stablecoins, the FCM must submit revised Regulation 1.11 risk-management policies and procedures to MPD via WinJammer before accepting the asset as customer margin collateral.
cftc_26_05_constraints.unresolved: CFM's actual notice-of-intent date, first customer-acceptance date, XRP-specific revised risk-policy filing and any weekly WinJammer asset reports were not located in public search. The initial three-month restriction and the start/end of weekly reporting therefore cannot be calculated.
caveats: The 20% minimum in CFTC Letter 26-05 is the customer-collateral fallback for a non-security digital asset such as XRP when it is not accepted by a registered DCO or a qualifying foreign clearing organization, subject to the letter's inverse-contract exception.

This is distinct from the September 2026 FAQ's separate 20% capital charge for FCM proprietary inventory positions in BTC/ETH and 2% for proprietary payment-stablecoin residual interest. Those proprietary-position figures do not establish an XRP customer-collateral haircut.

If CFM accepts XRP as margin collateral for a qualifying foreign clearing organization subject to the CPSS/IOSCO Recommendations for Central Counterparties, the applicable foreign clearing organization's haircut applies; Deribit's published 15% X:SM haircut is a candidate only if that qualification and CFM acceptance are established.
Deribit cross-collateral eligibility and CFM's regulatory no-action pathway do not prove that CFM has enabled XRP collateral or that any customer has posted XRP.

facts: CFM planned to offer Deribit Futures, Deribit Options and Deribit Perpetuals to its 30.7 customers and represented that it would accept customer-owned digital commodities and payment stablecoins as margin.

The CFTC staff position permits the described transfer of customer digital assets from CFM to CBBM and then Deribit under a right of re-use, solely for margining or securing the relevant 30.7 customer foreign futures and foreign-option obligations.
CFM, CBBM and Deribit must remain wholly owned subsidiaries of Coinbase Global; required customer disclosures, acknowledgements, audit/SOC 2 availability and integrated risk/security controls apply.
The no-action position requires compliance with all relevant CFTC Letter 26-05 asset-eligibility and haircut conditions.
CFTC Regulation 30.7 limits 30.7 customer funds deposited with CBBM to no more than 120% of required margin on the relevant customer positions.
caveats: The letter is a staff interpretation/no-action position, not a generally applicable Commission rule; it is not binding on the Commission or other staff and may be modified, suspended or terminated.
The route does not authorize unrelated use of customer assets; right-of-reuse is limited to the specified margin/security obligations.
The letter describes CFM's plan and representations; it does not disclose actual XRP collateral balances.

facts: Deribit lists XRP_USDC linear European options, quoted and margined in USDC; one option contract represents 1,000 XRP.
Deribit lists XRP among Tier 1 linear perpetuals.
The XRP_USDC option and perpetual instruments are USDC-denominated, not XRP-denominated.
The September 28, 2026 cross-collateral schedule marks XRP as a cross-collateral currency.
The displayed XRP haircut is 15% in Cross Standard Margin (X:SM); the X:PM column shows no haircut.
The same specification says cross-collateral currencies may be used as margin for derivative positions with other settlement currencies.
Deribit's Standard Margin documentation says new accounts default to Segregated Standard Margin (S:SM).
caveats: XRP cross-collateral use requires the relevant cross-collateral account mode; venue-wide eligibility does not prove the CFM route has enabled that mode for customers.

The 15% Deribit X:SM haircut applies to the CFTC route only if Deribit qualifies as a foreign clearing organization subject to the CPSS/IOSCO Recommendations for Central Counterparties and CFM accepts XRP through that route. If XRP is not accepted by a qualifying DCO/FCO, CFTC Letter 26-05 requires a minimum 20% customer-collateral haircut under condition 1.2.3.2.
The separate CFTC FAQ 20% proprietary BTC/ETH capital charge is not the basis for the XRP customer-collateral fallback; the latter is stated directly in CFTC Letter 26-05.
No public XRP collateral balance or CFM-specific account configuration was found.

points: A customer posting already-owned XRP as margin is a transfer/encumbrance of existing inventory, not proof of a new XRP spot purchase.
A right of re-use allows collateral to be re-posted for the permitted obligations; it does not by itself create new net XRP supply demand.
The Coinbase Custody Trust Company asset-backing representation concerns net liquidating equity support, not net new XRP acquisition.

Potential price effects depend on new acquisition demand, reduced available float, collateral rehypothecation, rebalancing conversions, and liquidations; none can be inferred from the regulatory pathway alone.

competing_hypotheses.thesis: If CFM enables XRP collateral and customers acquire XRP specifically to fund margin, institutional demand and custody balances could rise.
missing_proof: new spot purchases attributable to CFM customers

competing_hypotheses.thesis: Customers may post XRP already held in custody, reducing available inventory without generating new spot purchases.
Cross-collateral rebalancing could convert XRP with positive equity into a negative settlement currency during account stress, creating mechanical XRP sell/conversion flow.
missing_proof: Deribit rebalancing transactions by source asset
CFM account mode and collateral mix

competing_hypotheses.thesis: USDC and potentially RLUSD may be easier collateral choices, reducing the need to post XRP even while XRP remains eligible in principle.
missing_proof: actual stablecoin versus XRP collateral composition

unresolved_questions: What date did CFM file its 26-05 notice of intent, and what was its commencement date?
Has CFM submitted revised risk-management policies specifically covering XRP?
Has CFM made XRP available as collateral for 30.7 customers using Deribit?
Does CFM apply Deribit's 15% X:SM haircut, or the CFTC 26-05 minimum 20% fallback?
Is X:SM cross-collateral mode available to CFM customers, given Deribit's default S:SM account mode?
Are there public aggregate weekly collateral reports or a public CFTC filing showing XRP amounts?
What are the actual customer XRP balances held at Coinbase Custody Trust Company and the amount posted or re-used at Deribit?

Does Deribit qualify as a foreign clearing organization subject to the CPSS/IOSCO Recommendations for Central Counterparties for the specific 30.7 customer collateral route, and has CFM accepted it as such?

forecast.reason: A legal/technical collateral pathway is not a price signal. No XRP collateral balances, customer uptake, net spot acquisition or historical event response series has been verified.

handoff.next_action: Obtain the CFM notice-of-intent date and verify any public weekly asset reports or XRP-specific revised risk-policy filings before classifying XRP collateral as live.
